summary: jwt-logger@2.5.0 is an obfuscated import-time dropper impersonating a known author
details: On require('jwt-logger'), the package's main file jwt-logger.js executes a heavily obfuscated top-level IIFE that creates a hidden working directory under os.homedir(), writes an obfuscated second-stage JavaScript payload plus a generated package.json, invokes the resolved npm binary to install axios, better-sqlite3, node-machine-id, and socket.io-client (with ffi-napi and koffi added on Windows) into that directory, and then spawns node to execute the dropped payload. All literals, including require targets, directory names, the generated package.json contents, and the second-stage payload string, are hidden behind an obfuscator.io-style rotated string array and base64 decoder. The declared exports (jwtLog / createLog) implement no JWT-logging functionality and are unreachable; the package.json reuses Blake Embrey's name, email, and homepage and the README references blakeembrey/jwt-logger to impersonate a known maintainer. The second-stage dependency set (socket.io-client for a bidirectional C2 channel, node-machine-id for host fingerprinting, better-sqlite3 for reading local SQLite stores such as browser/wallet databases, ffi-napi/koffi on Windows for DPAPI-based credential decryption) is the fingerprint of an infostealer family. The exact C2 endpoint is embedded inside the encoded second-stage blob.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
